title: Overview
text:
Build with Cerberus. 
 One handheld. Two processors. A practical reference for writing firmware, connecting peripherals, and creating expansion boards. 
 Start developing  ↗ Explore the pinouts 

 ESP32-S3 Application + interface ESP32-C5 Dual-band radio coprocessor 320 × 480 ST7796 + GT911 touch 16 MB / 2 MB Production S3 flash / PSRAM 

 The device, documented. 
 Cerberus pairs a touchscreen application processor with an independently programmable radio processor. The S3 handles the display, touch, storage, USB, and user interface. The C5 handles radio work and exchanges structured messages over SPI. Different firmware can make use of the same hardware. 
 Display · Touch · microSD · USB · Battery gauge APPLICATION PROCESSOR ESP32-S3 SPI2 display / SDMMC storage / shared I²C SPI3 data + READY  UART for programming RADIO COPROCESSOR ESP32-C5 2.4 / 5 GHz Wi-Fi · Bluetooth LE · 802.15.4 

 Find what you need 
 01 / HARDWARE Every built-in connection GPIO tables, bus ownership, I²C addresses, and the S3-to-C5 link. 02 / FIRMWARE Program both processors Production memory settings, toolchain, protocol, and first-build checks. 03 / EXPANSION Make room for more Six-radio expansion, peripheral plans, and a dedicated KiCad file area. 04 / COMPATIBILITY Power it with confidence Tested batteries and dimensional candidates kept in separate lists. 05 / RF Match the right antenna Band coverage, connectors, cables, and repeatable test records. 06 / SUPPORT Get back to building USB recovery and checks for C5, display, SD, and battery readings. 

 Know your hardware revision 
 The baseline here is the production  N16R2  device with one onboard C5 and  1-bit SDMMC . The six-C5 expansion and Arcade wiring are separate configurations. GPS and RF/NFC add-ons are expansion features, not built-in parts of the base device. 
 Each guide distinguishes source-confirmed mappings, recorded hardware tests, and plans. Battery model validation, exact antenna connector part numbers, and an as-built expansion-header orientation still need records before they can be presented as confirmed compatibility. See  revisions and evidence . 
 A developer reference without device schematics. Pin assignments, software interfaces, and expansion information are published here. Cerberus main-board design files are excluded.

title: Start here
text:
Start developing 
 Start with the production N16R2 board profile, a USB data cable, and a known firmware release. Keep the onboard S3 and C5 images from the same release. 
 1. Identify your device 
 Record the board revision, S3 memory suffix, installed expansion board, and firmware version. The production reference has 16 MB S3 flash and 2 MB quad PSRAM. The C5 memory baseline is WROOM N4:  4 MB flash and no PSRAM . An S3 R8 development profile is a different target. 
 The device is independently programmable on both processors. The USB connection reaches the S3. A temporary S3 bridge exposes the onboard C5 for programming through that same connector. 
 2. Install a working baseline 
 Open the  Cerberus USB Installer  in a supported desktop browser and follow its S3 bridge → C5 → final S3 sequence. The final S3 application must be installed and verified before the device is ready to use. The  installer repository  contains maintenance information. 
 Use a data-capable USB cable. Close applications that hold the serial port. The port can change when the bridge appears or the S3 returns to its ROM downloader. 
 3. Get the firmware source 
 The public  Cerberus Sentinel repository  provides a working production implementation of display, touch, battery status, SD, USB, and the S3/C5 link. This Dev Board repository contains reference material and small examples; it is not a complete firmware image. 
 git clone https://github.com/463N7/Cerberus-Sentinel.git
cd Cerberus-Sentinel
python -m pip install platformio==6.1.19
python tools/build_sentinel.py --target all --package
 
 These build commands do not program your device. Consult the firmware repository's  build and recovery guide  for its current release workflow. See  programming  for memory and driver constraints. 
 4. Confirm the built-in features 
 
 S3 boots and reports the expected version and memory. 
 LCD orientation, colors, and backlight are correct; touch works at each corner. 
 Onboard C5 is online with the matched protocol/firmware version. 
 A known FAT32 card mounts and passes a controlled file read/write test. 
 Battery voltage and percentage are plausible, or the unavailable state is shown clearly. 
 USB remains usable after resetting and cold power-cycling. 
 
 Begin expansion work only after these baseline checks pass. Keep a recovery image and record the original pin assignments. 
 Recover the S3 USB connection 
 
 Hold the board's  S3 BOOT  control. 
 Tap  RESET  while keeping BOOT held. 
 Release BOOT, select the native S3 USB port, and reinstall the final S3 firmware. 
 Reset or power-cycle into the application and confirm its version. 
 
 This recovery path is documented for Cerberus. Physical board controls must be identified on your actual revision; their positions are not inferred from a generic ESP32 development board. 
 Next steps 
 Use the  built-in pinouts , choose an  expansion profile , and work through the  programming guide . Record hardware results using the compatibility-report forms linked from the repository.

 The C5 memory specification uses the smallest standard WROOM configuration listed by Espressif:  N4, with 4 MB Quad SPI flash and no PSRAM . This applies to the memory baseline for both WROOM-1 and WROOM-1U; it does not select the device's antenna variant. Firmware can use a smaller partition layout within that capacity. 
 The C5 silicon supports the listed radio families; an installed application may expose only a subset. Support for 802.15.4 does not itself establish a complete Zigbee or Thread application. The base device has no built-in LoRa, CC1101, nRF24, NFC reader, or GPS in this reference.

 Electrical and mechanical reference 
 Treat S3/C5 signals as  3.3 V logic . Do not connect 5 V signal outputs directly or infer supply capability from a GPIO label. Verify a peripheral's logic voltage separately from its supply input. 
 Keep GPIO19/20 for USB, memory pins for flash/PSRAM, and GPIO0/3/45/46 startup strapping requirements intact. Do not treat an unassigned GPIO as physically exposed or safe to repurpose. The production SD pull-up network means GPIO38 is not an SD control in the production firmware. 
 The following need board-specific measurement before being advertised: expansion-rail current limits, charger input/charge limits, battery connector part number/polarity, enclosure battery cavity, board outline, mounting holes, antenna connector part numbers, and physical header numbering. A component's datasheet maximum is not the assembled board's rating.

Confirm GPIO output capability, startup straps, physical exposure, power, firmware support, and module suffixes against the actual expansion design before implementation. 
 Shared-bus development rules 
 
 Register each SPI device with its own CS, clock rate, mode, and bit order. Do not apply the C5's 40 MHz setting to every peripheral. 
 Serialize complete request/response sequences when the protocol requires it; preserve the C5 READY handshake when using Sentinel's link. 
 Make every unused CS inactive before starting the bus. Use board-appropriate reset bias on selects and enables while preserving S3 startup straps. 
 For a proposed expander, set its output latch to the desired state before enabling output directions. Slow I²C control signals are not substitutes for precise pulse capture or SPI clocks. 
 Keep radio power separate from GPIO control. The E01 suffix changes peak current and footprint; the prior 2 A and 3 A supply proposals were design budgets, not measured Cerberus expansion-rail ratings. 
 Power off before attaching/removing a board. Isolate or remove add-ons using GPIO43 before C5 programming. 
 
 KiCad files have a home 
 Use  hardware/expansion/  for expansion  PCB/project files, footprints, and release notes . Add each design in a revision-named folder and include connector orientation, supported Cerberus revision, power budget, assembly notes, and validation status. 
 No CAD files have been added yet. Main-device CAD and all schematic files are excluded. A folder is not a manufacturing release; only label a revision “tested” when there is a matching validation record.

title: Programming
text:
Programming reference 
 The S3 runs application services. The onboard C5 runs a separate radio application. Their shared wire interface and protocol must agree; changing one processor's firmware can require rebuilding both. 
 Reference toolchain 
 The recorded production Sentinel toolchain is PlatformIO Core  6.1.19 , platform  espressif32@7.0.1 , and  ESP-IDF 6.0.1  ( framework-espidf@4.60001.0 ). Use the pinned configuration and dependency lock files in the firmware repository. 
 # Run inside a Cerberus-Sentinel checkout.
python tools/build_sentinel.py --target s3
python tools/build_sentinel.py --target c5
python tools/build_sentinel.py --target bridge
python tools/build_sentinel.py --target all --package
 
 Memory and partitions 
 
 
 
 Target 
 Reference memory profile 
 Application partition 
 
 
 
 
 Production S3 
 16 MB flash, DIO 80 MHz; 2 MB quad PSRAM 
 0x10000 , size  0x700000  in Sentinel 
 
 
 Onboard C5 
 4 MB flash / no PSRAM (WROOM N4 baseline); current Sentinel layout uses 2 MB 
 0x10000 , size  0x1F0000  in Sentinel 
 
 
 Temporary S3 bridge 
 Production S3 profile 
 Uses the S3 application slot temporarily 
 
 
 
 The C5 hardware reference is the smallest standard C5-WROOM memory option:  4 MB flash and no PSRAM . Sentinel's current 2 MB image layout is a software allocation within that capacity, not the module's physical flash specification. These offsets belong to the referenced firmware layout. Use each release's manifest and partition images when flashing; partition changes require rebuilding and validation. 
 Keep production PSRAM in quad mode.  Octal PSRAM can reserve GPIO35–37 used by microSD. DMA buffers and task stacks must follow ESP-IDF memory requirements; large optional UI buffers can explicitly request PSRAM and handle allocation failure. 
 Source layout and driver entry points 
 
 
 
 Location in Sentinel 
 Responsibility 
 
 
 
 
 shared/cerberus_pins.h 
 Production board signal assignments

 Shared message definitions, framing, capabilities, versions

 Temporary USB/UART bridge

 Onboard C5 application 
 
 
 
 Use those driver implementations when integrating into the same firmware. Adding a second independent SPI or I²C owner over existing pins will break the shared services. 
 S3/C5 protocol 
 The current Sentinel header identifies protocol  V2 , with V1 fallback and a capability bitmap. Ordinary framed transfers are  32 bytes  with a  22-byte payload ; event batches have a separate  64-byte  transfer form. V2 framing includes CRC validation and bounded payload handling. Use the exact structures and helpers from the matching firmware commit. 
 The normal READY line is  C5 GPIO11 → S3 GPIO44 . It reuses the C5 UART TX wire. Before clocking a request, the S3 waits for a queued C5 transfer; request/response timing and fallback handling belong to the link driver. The UART is not the normal runtime message path. 
 The legacy seven-radio scanner uses different framing and IRQ behavior. Do not treat an identical SPI pinout as protocol compatibility. 
 C5 programming through the S3 
 The bridge temporarily occupies the S3 application slot, sets C5 boot/reset control, and forwards USB to the C5 UART at  115200 baud, 8N1 . The established path uses the esptool stub, uncompressed writes, and  4096-byte blocks . 
 
 
 
 Host-facing interface 
 USB VID:PID 
 Role 
 
 
 
 
 Native S3 USB Serial/JTAG 
 303A:1001 
 Install bridge or final S3 firmware 
 
 
 Cerberus C5 flash bridge 
 303A:4001 
 Reach onboard C5 ROM loader 
 
 
 
 The bridge's USB line-coding requests are firmware-specific: 2400 requests C5 ROM reset/retry, 1200 returns to S3 ROM, and 9600 returns carrier identity. They do not change the physical C5 UART rate. Use the  full bridge contract  before writing a custom programmer. Compare device identity across port changes and always reinstall the final S3 application. 
 Battery gauge integration 
 Use the existing shared bus at 400 kHz and MAX17048 address  0x36 . Its voltage register is  0x02 , state-of-charge register  0x04 , and version register  0x08 . Words are read most-significant byte first. The documented conversions are  78.125 µV per VCELL count  and  1/256 percent per SOC count . See the  Analog Devices datasheet . 
 Sentinel samples every 5 seconds, retries unavailable readings after 30 seconds, and exposes a cached read-only  battery  console command. A voltage or SOC reading is not proof of battery presence or charging. BQ25895 charging-state support is a separate charger integration; its actual configuration is not defined by the gauge driver. 
 Bring-up sequence for a new application 
 
 Boot the correct memory profile and preserve native USB recovery. 
 Bring up LCD, shared I²C, touch, and gauge without expansion attached. 
 Initialize the C5 control pins, release reset, and validate protocol/capabilities. 
 Mount and test SD with 1-bit SDMMC; never format an existing card automatically. 
 Add one expansion device at a time with a unique select and correct bus settings. 
 Repeat after cold power-cycling, with battery power, and with all intended peripherals present. 
 
 The  examples folder  contains a standalone pin header and a read-only I²C identification example. It is not a complete BSP or a claim that a new binary was tested on hardware.

title: Batteries
text:
Batteries 
 Battery compatibility has two separate questions:  does it fit , and  has it been tested electrically in this device ? A capacity label or similar-looking connector does not answer either question completely. 
 Tested batteries 
 No exact battery model is yet documented in this public reference.  Prior board discussions describe operation with a battery installed, and recorded firmware checks show a working MAX17048 reading. Neither record identifies a cell model, dimensions, connector polarity, charge rating, or runtime test, so neither is listed as a tested battery product.

 This section is reserved for candidates whose dimensions and connector have been compared with the actual enclosure and board. The battery cavity dimensions and connector part/polarity have not been recovered from the available records, so no product is marked “should fit” yet.

 “Should fit” will mean a dimensional candidate only. It must remain in this section until charging, operation, and enclosure fit have been recorded on a named revision. 
 What is known about battery support 
 
 The onboard  MAX17048  fuel gauge is at I²C address  0x36 . It provides voltage and an estimated percentage. 
 BQ25895  is the charger identified in the earlier Cerberus board design discussion. TI documents it as a single-cell charger; its configured limits on the assembled board still need a record. 
 The gauge's reading does not establish charging status. USB attachment alone does not establish charging status either. 
 The charger STAT LED is a charge/fault indicator, not a general device power light. LED-off and blinking states have more than one possible cause; inspect charger status before assigning a cause. 
 
 The  MAX17048 documentation  and  BQ25895 documentation  describe the components. They do not certify a particular battery or the assembled Cerberus board's charging limits. 
 A useful compatibility record 
 For each battery, record the manufacturer and exact SKU, product/datasheet link, chemistry/cell count, nominal and maximum charge voltage, rated capacity, allowed charge current, protection board, lead length, connector manufacturer/series/pitch, and a photo identifying positive and negative contacts. 
 Measure thickness, width, length, cable bend space, and installed clearance. Record board and enclosure revision, charger settings, USB source, firmware, brightness, radio workload, ambient temperature, starting charge, elapsed runtime, and the observed stop condition. Runtime estimates and completed discharge measurements belong in separate fields. 
 Use the  battery compatibility report . An exact model record can be added without publishing device schematics.

 Compact nRF24/E01 form factor 
 Candidate preference recorded; exact model/connector not identified 
 
 
 
 These are recovered planning candidates, not purchasing recommendations or tested substitutes. No current price, stock, or delivery claim is made. 
 Installation and comparison records 
 Record antenna part number, manufacturer datasheet, band, nominal impedance, connector, cable type/length, mounting location, keep-out/ground-plane requirements, and enclosure revision. For an active GNSS antenna, additionally record its permitted supply voltage/current and whether the expansion board supplies antenna bias. 
 Compare with the same Cerberus board, firmware, radio settings, antenna orientation, location, reference source, and test duration. Save observations separately for each band. RSSI alone is not an antenna-gain measurement, and a single reception result does not establish range or full-band performance. 
 Use the  antenna compatibility report . A simple installed photo and exact part number are useful first additions.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting 
 Identify the board revision and installed firmware before applying a fix. The production device, historical scanner prototype, and Arcade build use different memory and peripheral configurations. 
 
 
 
 Symptom 
 Check first 
 Useful next step 
 
 
 
 
 No USB port 
 Data cable, direct USB connection, serial app holding the port 
 Use S3 BOOT + RESET recovery and select the native S3 endpoint 
 
 
 Port disappears during installation 
 Bridge and native USB have different identities 
 Follow the installer port prompts; reinstall final S3 firmware after C5 
 
 
 S3 stays in bridge / loader 
 Final application not installed or normal boot not requested 
 Recover S3, program the final image, then reset and confirm version 
 
 
 C5 offline 
 Matched S3/C5 images, C5 reset state, READY44 
 Inspect protocol/version health; do not attach another output to GPIO44 
 
 
 C5 flash fails partway 
 Stable supply, 115200 baud, supported bridge settings 
 Use the documented retry path and 4096-byte write blocks 
 
 
 Blank or wrong-color LCD 
 Correct ST7796 driver, SPI2 pins, backlight, panel orientation 
 Restore a known production firmware before changing wiring 
 
 
 Touch not detected 
 Shared I²C GPIO8/9, GT911 address 0x5D, INT7 
 Check bus access; cold power-cycle because touch reset is not connected 
 
 
 SD unavailable 
 FAT32 card, full power-cycle, correct 1-bit SDMMC mode 
 Check GPIO35/36/37 and quad PSRAM; production does not drive GPIO38 
 
 
 SD files corrupt or inaccessible over USB 
 Card ownership during USB mass-storage mode 
 Eject on the host before returning it to the device's file service 
 
 
 Battery shows --% 
 Gauge detection at 0x36 and last read error 
 Use the firmware battery console status; do not substitute a fake percentage 
 
 
 Charger LED is off or flashes 
 Actual battery and charger status 
 STAT is not a power LED; distinguish no charge, completion, and faults from registers 
 
 
 Expansion module fails or causes brownout 
 Correct profile, module side pin map, stable board supply 
 Add one module at a time; a USB-UART adapter may not power a multi-radio bank 
 
 
 Two SPI devices stop responding 
 CS states, shared bus ownership, per-device mode/clock/bit order 
 Verify deselection and MISO release before testing concurrent workloads 
 
 
 
 A helpful issue report 
 Include board and enclosure revision, firmware version/commit, S3 memory type, attached expansion revision, power source, exact peripheral model, steps to reproduce, expected behavior, and diagnostic output with private identifiers removed. 
 For physical pin questions, include a connector photo with viewing side and pin 1 marked. Do not upload main-device schematics, fabrication files, memory dumps, credentials, or captured network data to this documentation repository. 
 Open a documentation or hardware-reference issue .

title: Revisions + evidence
text:
Revisions and evidence 
 This reference was assembled on  October 27, 2026  from the current public Sentinel source, local production/scanner records, and earlier Cerberus hardware discussions. Source-confirmed pin assignments, hardware observations, and proposed designs are different evidence levels. 
 Reference baseline 
 The public source baseline is  Cerberus Sentinel commit 580c80d . It provides the production pin map, toolchain, memory configuration, driver behavior, and C5 bridge contract. Upstream changes do not automatically change the baseline in these docs. 
 
 
 
 Record 
 What it establishes 
 What it does not establish 
 
 
 
 
 Production pin definitions 
 LCD, touch, SDMMC, S3/C5 SPI and READY signals 
 Physical connector position or every unit's assembly 
 
 
 C5 memory specification 
 WROOM N4 baseline: 4 MB flash / no PSRAM, the smallest standard listed C5-WROOM memory option 
 A requirement for larger-memory modules; Sentinel's 2 MB firmware layout is a separate software allocation 
 
 
 First-board flash record, October 11 
 One S3 detected with 16 MB flash / 2 MB PSRAM; both processors programmed and verified 
 The memory specification for all production units 
 
 
 Later battery/health verification 
 MAX17048 available with plausible voltage/SOC; later SD mount success recorded 
 Exact battery SKU, charging limits, runtime, or cell-presence sensing 
 
 
 Six-C5 programming record, September 29 
 Six 4 MB WROOM modules passed write verification 
 Completed cold-cycle seven-radio scan acceptance 
 
 
 Earlier Rev A design discussion 
 BQ25895 charger identification and STAT LED discussion 
 Full recovered charger settings or exact battery product list 
 
 
 Revised SDMMC routing discussion 
 GPIO38 expansion routing, SD on GPIO35/36/37 
 A complete physical header orientation record 
 
 
 RF/NFC expansion planning 
 E01/E07/PN532/GPS and later CC1101/expander proposals 
 Fabricated board, verified pinout, or working firmware support 
 
 
 
 Revision boundaries 
 
 Production N16R2:  default device reference. Quad PSRAM, SDMMC 1-bit, ST7796/GT911, and onboard C5. 
 Prototype SD wiring:  GPIO38 may be tied to DAT3/CS. Check the actual routing before reuse. 
 R8 Arcade development:  octal memory and additional controls/audio are application-specific. Arcade audio on GPIO11/12/13 overlaps the C5 SPI bus; buttons also overlap expansion and GPS signals. These are not extra built-in features of the baseline board. 
 WROOM versus XIAO expansion:  different MOSI/MISO/CS mappings, separate firmware targets. 
 
 Next records to add 
 
 Base-board revision label and clear connector photos with pin 1 and viewing side. 
 A continuity-verified physical expansion-header map, mating connector, and power pin ratings. 
 Exact battery connector and polarity, charger configured limits, enclosure cavity measurements, and known battery SKUs. 
 Antenna module/connector part numbers and a tested antenna table with band-specific results. 
 Expansion KiCad PCB releases, mechanical outline, assembly notes, and validation logs. 
 A small standalone board-support project with a repeatable display/touch/SD/C5 test procedure. 
 
 Documentation changelog 
 
 
 
 Date 
 Change 
 
 
 
 
 2026-10-27 
 Initial Cerberus Dev Board reference; production pinouts, expansion profiles, programming/recovery, battery/antenna record structures, and separate expansion CAD area 
 
 
 2026-10-27 
 Set the C5 hardware memory baseline to the smallest standard WROOM option: N4, 4 MB flash and no PSRAM; distinguish the current 2 MB firmware layout 
 
 
 
 Use the  documentation issue form  to submit an exact correction and its evidence. Hardware test claims should name the board revision, firmware, date, and test conditions.
